doc.title: Marty Grosz interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995

title: First record bought: Paging the Devil
summary: His first purchased jazz record, by Lester Young, Buck Clayton and the Basie rhythm section; he bought it for the title.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: No. That was without Basie. With Eddie Durham on electric guitar, Freddie Green, Walter Page, Jo Jones, the Basie rhythm section without Basie. Contractual reasons obviously. And then Buck Clayton and Lester Young. And the only reason, I didn’t know any of these guys, the only reason I bought the record was because of the title, you know I hadn’t heard it and I said, “Paging the Devil,” wow, that sounds real evil and funky and stuff. And it turned out it was because Walter Page playing the blues and he had a band called the Blue Devils. So that’s how that all, as you well know, doing your Basie stuff.
Well if that was your first record, then you had a great introduction—
It’s not the first record I heard, but that I actually bought for myself.
Well you had a good thing to listen to with Freddie Green.
